te: Study visit to the Army Ordnance Department prepared
se: The meeting prepared a study visit to the Army Ordnance Department, Bangkok, on 24 July 2025, to study its capacity to produce and repair weapons, visit the rifle and barrel factory, and hear the department's views, direction and limits
it: Study visit to the Army Ordnance Department, 24 July 2025

te: Amendments to laws that are obstacles to exporting military equipment followed up
se: The meeting considered how to follow up amendments to laws relating to the defence industry, especially the approval process for exporting military equipment made by the private sector, which until now has had to go to the Council of Ministers each time and takes a long time, and stressed the importance of a complete industry database classified by level and industry group
it: Amending laws that are obstacles to exporting military equipment
Building a database and standards for the defence industry

te: The armed forces explain how they are updating their organisation and equipment tables to keep up with the situation
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Directorate of Joint Operations and the operations departments of the Royal Thai Army, Navy and Air Force to give information on updating the armed forces' tables of organisation and equipment (TO&E). In summary, fast-changing technology means that ways of fighting and force structures must adapt
it: Updating the armed forces' tables of organisation and equipment (TO&E)

te: Annual report of the Defence Technology Institute considered
se: The meeting considered the 2023 annual report of the Defence Technology Institute (DTI), the Ministry of Defence's main agency for research and development of defence technology, which aims to build self-reliance, reduce imports and push forward production of military equipment in Thailand
it: Annual report 2023 of the Defence Technology Institute

te: Joint meeting with the committee: approaches to supporting budgets for developing the defence industry
se: The subcommittee met jointly with the Committee on Military Affairs and State Security to hear approaches to pushing for and supporting budgets to develop the defence industry, such as supporting armed forces research so that prototypes go into use and are scaled up to industry, with the agencies concerned invited to give information
it: Approaches to pushing for and supporting budgets to develop the defence industry

te: State agencies' capacity to produce firearms and ammunition heard
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Weapon Production Center, the Defence Industry and Energy Center and the Defence Technology Institute to give information on their capacity to produce firearms and ammunition and on problems and obstacles, such as production capacity and demand for artillery ammunition, plans to upgrade production lines, and rifle research and development
it: Capacity to produce firearms and ammunition, and problems and obstacles

te: Report prepared for presentation to the Senate, and study topics on unmanned systems and AI set
se: The meeting prepared to present the report "Defence Industry Capabilities, Challenges and Opportunities for Thailand" to the Senate on 1 April 2025, and discussed further study topics, such as unmanned systems in the air, on land and at sea, and the military use of artificial intelligence
it: Report: defence industry capabilities, challenges and opportunities for Thailand
Next study topics: unmanned systems, and artificial intelligence in military use

te: Lop Buri study visit summarised, and the committee's observations on the report noted
se: Agenda: Key points from the study visit on the defence industry, Lop Buri Province, 6–7 March 2025 (the Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda in the meeting notice, not a resolution of the meeting)
it: Key points from the study visit on the defence industry, Lop Buri Province, 6–7 March 2025
The committee's observations on the subcommittee's study report

te: BOI gives information on investment incentives in the defence industry
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Office of the Board of Investment (BOI) to give information on investment promotion in 4 groups of the defence industry: producing and repairing vehicles and weapon systems, unmanned vehicles, weapons and training aids, and combat support equipment, which receive tax and non-tax incentives. The meeting gave observations so that promotion continues
it: Approaches to promoting investment in the defence industry

te: The Defence Industry and Energy Center and the Office of Industrial Economics explain plans to develop the defence industry
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Defence Industry and Energy Center, Ministry of Defence, and the Office of Industrial Economics, Ministry of Industry, to explain the integrated plan for developing the defence industry, to follow its progress, direction, policy and obstacles, including exports and self-reliance. Thailand's capacity to produce military equipment such as firearms, armoured vehicles, warships and unmanned aircraft was presented
it: Integrated plan for developing the defence industry

te: Study visit to Lop Buri prepared, and a seminar to promote the defence industry planned
se: The meeting noted the schedule of the Senate's study visit on food security strategy and the development of the defence industry in Lop Buri Province on 6–7 March 2025, which representatives of the subcommittee will join, and considered preparations for a seminar to promote the defence industry
it: Study visit to Lop Buri Province, 6–7 March 2025
Preparations for a seminar to promote the defence industry

te: Representatives sent for discussions with Royal Thai Navy and Royal Thai Army Headquarters
se: The meeting approved 3 representatives of the subcommittee to travel for discussions at Royal Thai Navy Headquarters on 27 February 2025 and at Royal Thai Army Headquarters
it: Representatives of the subcommittee join discussions at Royal Thai Navy and Royal Thai Army Headquarters

te: Report on defence industry capabilities in 7 domains followed up
se: The meeting noted progress on the study report on defence industry capabilities for combat power in all 7 domains, to propose approaches to developing Thai industry, and considered the draft report proposing a structure and framework for a study to develop national security and military affairs, as assigned by the committee, asking subcommittee members to study it and give observations at the next meeting
it: Study report: defence industry capabilities for combat power in 7 domains
Draft report proposing a structure and framework for a study to develop national security and military affairs

te: The Defence Technology Institute heard on the direction of the defence industry
se: Agenda: The direction of Thailand's defence industry, opportunities and challenges (representatives of the Defence Technology Institute invited) (the Senate has not yet published the summary of this meeting, so this text is the agenda in the meeting notice, not a resolution of the meeting)
it: The direction of Thailand's defence industry, opportunities and challenges (representatives of the Defence Technology Institute invited)

te: Discussion with the Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Thai Navy summarised, and the idea of using drones for logistics
se: The meeting summarised its discussion with the Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Thai Navy on 9 January 2025, which agreed on procuring frigates built in Thailand, and discussed the ideas of using drones for logistics in remote areas (subject to the relevant regulations), leasing rather than buying military equipment to reduce the maintenance burden, and setting up a centre to safeguard national interests in space
it: Summary of the discussion with the Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Thai Navy on frigates
Using drones for logistics in remote areas
Acquiring military equipment by leasing instead of buying
The idea of setting up a centre to safeguard national interests in space

te: The Royal Thai Navy heard on building frigates in Thailand
se: The meeting invited representatives of the Naval Operations Department, the Naval Dockyard Department and the Naval Ordnance Department to give information on the Royal Thai Navy's approach to procuring equipment, and noted the need to procure frigates in fiscal year 2026 and the benefits of building ships in Thailand for national defence, law enforcement and helping the public, diplomacy, personnel training and the development of domestic industry
it: The Royal Thai Navy's approach to procuring equipment, and procuring frigates built in Thailand
